title: 8 Hidden iPhone Settings Beginners Should Turn On
hook: Your iPhone can do far more than most people ever discover. A few settings, hidden deep in the menus, can protect your phone, save your battery, free up storage and make daily use faster. Here are eight to switch on today, and each takes less than a minute. None of it needs any technical knowledge. We also cover what to do if you cannot find a setting.
intro: Apple builds many useful features into every iPhone, but it doesn't always switch them on for you. Some protect you if your phone is stolen, some stretch the life of your battery, and some simply save time. We'll walk through each setting, show exactly where to find it, and explain why it matters. Menu names can differ a little between iOS versions, so if you cannot find one, use the search bar at the top of Settings.
youNeedNarration: Here's what you need. Your iPhone, updated to a recent version of iOS if possible. Your passcode, since some settings ask for it. Your Apple Account signed in, and a few minutes of your time. Nothing needs to be downloaded, and you can switch any of these off again whenever you like.
heroImagePrompt: A person holding an iPhone showing the Settings app with a list of toggles, bright home setting, shallow depth of field, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Turn on Back Tap
steps.narration: Step one. Open Settings, then Accessibility, Touch, and scroll down to Back Tap. Choose Double Tap or Triple Tap, and assign an action, like Screenshot, Flashlight, or Control Center. Now you can tap the back of your phone twice, and it will perform that action, even with a case on. It's a quick shortcut when your hands are full, or when you want to take a screenshot without pressing two buttons at once. Try it right now. If it doesn't respond at first, tap a little firmer on the lower half of the back, and test again.
steps.tip: Double tap the back for a screenshot
steps.mistake: Assigning too many shortcuts at once
steps.imagePrompt: A finger tapping the back of an iPhone held in one hand, bright indoor light, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Switch on Stolen Device Protection
steps.narration: Step two. Go to Settings, Face ID and Passcode, enter your passcode, and scroll to Stolen Device Protection. Turn it on. This feature, available on recent versions of iOS, adds extra security when your iPhone is away from familiar places such as your home or work. For sensitive actions, like changing your Apple Account password, it requires Face ID, and sometimes a security delay. Even if someone learns your passcode, your account stays safer. Check that your Apple Account has a trusted phone number, so you can recover it if you need to.
steps.mistake: Skipping security because it seems unnecessary
steps.imagePrompt: An iPhone showing a security settings screen with a padlock icon, held in a hand, soft light, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Enable Send Last Location
steps.narration: Step three. Open Settings, tap your name at the top, choose Find My, then Find My iPhone, and make sure Find My network and Send Last Location are both switched on. Send Last Location shares your iPhone's position with Apple when the battery is almost empty, so you can still find it later. Find My network helps locate your phone even when it's offline, using nearby Apple devices. It takes thirty seconds and could save you the cost of a new phone. Make sure Location Services is switched on as well, and set up Find My on every Apple device you own.
steps.tip: Find My works even when offline
steps.imagePrompt: An iPhone showing a map with a location pin, held by a person at a café table, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Use Optimized Battery Charging
steps.narration: Step four. Go to Settings, Battery, and look for Charging, or Battery Health and Charging, depending on your version. Switch on Optimized Battery Charging. Your iPhone learns your routine, and pauses charging at around eighty percent, finishing the last part just before you usually unplug. This reduces wear on the battery over the years. On newer models you may also find a charge limit option, which keeps the battery at a lower level on purpose. If you use a fast charger or an older iPhone, the option may be under a slightly different name.
steps.tip: Slower charging keeps the battery healthier
steps.mistake: Leaving the phone at one hundred percent for days
steps.imagePrompt: An iPhone charging on a bedside table with a lamp glowing softly in the evening, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Offload unused apps
steps.narration: Step five. Open Settings, then App Store, and turn on Offload Unused Apps. When your storage runs low, your iPhone removes apps you haven't opened in a while, but keeps their documents and data. The app icon stays on your screen with a small cloud, so you can tap it to download it again. This is a painless way to free up gigabytes without losing anything. You can also check Settings, General, iPhone Storage for suggestions. If you want an app back, simply tap its icon, and wait a few seconds for the download.
steps.tip: Data stays, only the app is removed
steps.mistake: Deleting photos instead of unused apps
steps.imagePrompt: An iPhone storage screen with a colorful usage bar and a list of apps, held in a hand, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Create text shortcuts
steps.narration: Step six. Go to Settings, General, Keyboard, then Text Replacement, and tap the plus button. In the Phrase box, type something long, like your email address, home address or a common reply. In Shortcut, type a few letters, like email or omw. From now on, when you type that shortcut, your iPhone offers the full phrase, and one tap fills it in. It saves hundreds of keystrokes every week, and it is perfect for long addresses. Start with the two or three phrases you type most often, such as your name or your phone number.
steps.tip: Type omw, get a full sentence
steps.mistake: Using a shortcut that is also a real word
steps.imagePrompt: Thumbs typing a message on an iPhone keyboard with a suggestion bar above the keys, soft light, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Schedule your notifications
steps.narration: Step seven. Notifications can fill your day with interruptions. Open Settings, then Notifications, then Scheduled Summary. Turn it on, choose the apps you want to include, and set one to three times a day when you would like to receive them. Your iPhone will gather less urgent notifications into one summary, instead of buzzing every few minutes. Important things, like calls and messages from people you choose, can still come through at once, if you set up a Focus. Pick times that suit you, such as just after breakfast and mid-evening. You can change them any time.
steps.tip: Two summaries a day is plenty
steps.mistake: Putting every app in the summary
steps.imagePrompt: An iPhone lock screen showing a tidy stack of notifications, resting on a wooden desk, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Turn on automatic updates
steps.narration: Step eight. Open Settings, General, Software Update, and tap Automatic Updates. Switch on both Download iOS Updates and Install iOS Updates. Your iPhone will download new versions on Wi-Fi and install them overnight while charging. Updates include important security fixes that protect you from new threats, as well as improvements to performance. You will still be asked before major upgrades, in many cases. Keeping up to date is the single easiest way to stay safe. Restart your iPhone once a week as well. It is the oldest trick, and it keeps things running smoothly.
steps.imagePrompt: An iPhone showing a software update screen with a progress bar, charging on a desk at night, photorealistic, no text

bonus.label: TROUBLESHOOTING
bonus.title: Cannot find a setting?
bonus.narration: If a setting is missing, there are three common reasons. Menu names move around between versions, so use the search bar at the top of Settings. Some features need a recent phone or software: Back Tap needs an iPhone 8 or later, and Stolen Device Protection needs iOS 17.3 or later. If a switch is grayed out, a restriction or a work profile may control it.
bonus.tip: Use the search bar in Settings
bonus.imagePrompt: A hand holding an iPhone showing the Settings app with the search field at the top, a cup of coffee on a wooden table nearby, bright indoor light. 16:9 landscape format. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark.

bonus.label: GO FURTHER
bonus.title: Two safety extras
bonus.narration: Two more settings are worth a minute. First, set up your Medical ID in the Health app, with emergency contacts. Someone can see it from the lock screen in an emergency, even without your passcode. Second, turn on Silence Unknown Callers in the Phone settings, so calls from numbers not in your contacts go straight to voicemail. Both can be changed back at any time.
bonus.imagePrompt: A hand holding an iPhone showing a plain emergency information screen with a red cross symbol, sitting on a kitchen counter, soft daylight, nothing readable on the screen. 16:9 landscape format. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark.

bonus.label: PREVENTION
bonus.title: Back up your phone
bonus.narration: The best protection is a recent backup. Open Settings, tap your name, choose iCloud, then iCloud Backup, and turn it on. The phone will back up overnight when it is charging and connected to Wi-Fi. Turn on two-factor authentication for your Apple Account too. Never share your passcode or the verification codes sent to you. Apple will not call you and ask for them.
bonus.imagePrompt: An iPhone charging on a bedside table next to a small lamp at night, a glass of water beside it, warm light, screen showing only a dim lock screen with no text. 16:9 landscape format. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark.

mistakesToAvoid.narration: Before you go, three mistakes to avoid. First, turning on settings you don't understand. Read each description, and change one thing at a time. Second, ignoring security. Updates, Find My and Stolen Device Protection protect your photos and accounts. And third, never checking your storage until it's full. A little maintenance each month saves the stress of the dreaded storage full message at an awkward moment. None of these settings is permanent, so experiment freely.
items: Waiting until storage is completely full

recap.narration: Let's recap. Turn on Back Tap. Switch on Stolen Device Protection. Enable Find My and Send Last Location. Use Optimized Battery Charging. Offload unused apps. Create text shortcuts. Schedule your notifications. And turn on automatic updates. Eight settings, about five minutes, and an iPhone that is safer, tidier and faster to use. And if a setting is missing, search for it, and back up your phone.

outro: That's eight hidden iPhone settings worth turning on. If you found a new favorite, subscribe to WikiTube, because we publish a new how-to every single day. Tell us in the comments which setting surprised you most, and what you would like us to explain next. See you tomorrow.
